body:
Good morning, Kern County. Thursday’s news leads with an arrest tied to the east Bakersfield shooting that left two people dead, a break that the Sheriff’s Office announced overnight. The weather is cooperating for a calm start to the day: a high near 84, a current reading of 60 at Meadows Field, and no active weather alerts, though the air quality index sits at 53, a moderate number.

## The Kern Overnight

The overnight hours had one significant moment and it ended quietly. Just before 1 a.m., an officer broadcast a Code 33 — the radio signal that clears the channel for emergency traffic — while following a vehicle westbound on Hampton Avenue. Units called out their positions block by block as the vehicle appeared to yield, then made a quick correction on the location and confirmed the driver had stopped. Multiple officers arrived behind the scene, and once the stop was complete the channel was opened back to normal traffic.

The night’s most serious call came after 2:20 a.m., when officers and Liberty Ambulance paramedics were sent to a park on Hawthorne Avenue. Dispatch described a man in a black shirt and blue jeans with facial injuries who said he had been jumped. He was last seen walking eastbound on Hawthorne from the park, and a short time later an engine was cleared to an updated address on the same street as the response shifted.

Fire crews dealt with a familiar kind of nuisance late in the evening. Battalion 6 was sent to a refuse fire burning inside a decommissioned tank that crews recognized as one previously used for burning copper wire. The battalion downgraded the assignment and kept it with the companies already on scene rather than sending a larger response.

Other calls filled out the log. Officers were sent to an apartment in the 6200 block of Victor Street after a caller said a man and a woman were taking boards off the place and entering the residence. A prowler report at a car wash in the 8100 block of East Brundage Lane brought descriptions of a woman in a tie-dye shirt and black shorts and a man in a hunter-green ball cap, green shirt and blue jeans; dispatchers noted the pair might be connected to an earlier vandalism call. The broader log included a 9:32 p.m. welfare check on a Smith Street block, a 9:46 p.m. verbal disturbance on Breezeway Drive involving an ex-boyfriend who would not leave, a 10:07 p.m. battery report east of Haley Street and Panorama Drive in which security said a woman in her mid-twenties was belligerent and battering her friend, and just after 11 p.m. a semi reported stopped on the right-hand shoulder of a county highway.

## Today's weather

Forecasters expect a mild, comfortable Thursday across Kern County, with a high near 84 and an overnight low around 60. The current observation at Meadows Field is 60 degrees. There are no active weather alerts for the county, and no fires are listed in the current conditions update. Air quality is moderate at 53 on the Air Quality Index, which is fine for most people; those unusually sensitive to particulate matter may want to limit time outdoors through the afternoon.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield Now reports that the Kern County Sheriff’s Office has made an arrest in connection with the east Bakersfield shooting that left two people dead.** The announcement is a significant step in a case that has weighed on that part of town since the shooting happened. No additional details about the suspect, a possible motive or the charges were included in the report.

**According to 23ABC, the California Highway Patrol is searching for the driver of a 1990s-era pickup truck who struck a mother selling elotes near the FoodMaxx parking lot on Niles Street and then fled without stopping to help.** The victim, Silvia Soto, 46, was hit just before midnight on Sept. 11 and remains hospitalized after surgery. Her daughter, Esmeralda Morales, told the station that Soto spent long hours selling corn to provide for her four children and that the family has struggled emotionally and financially without her; Morales also pointed to tire marks still visible in the roadway at the scene of the crash.

**KGET 17 reports that community members are pressing Bakersfield leaders to end the city’s use of Flock license-plate cameras and to provide more transparency about how the surveillance system works.** The demand is part of an ongoing public debate over privacy and policing technology in Bakersfield. The report did not indicate whether the council is expected to take up the issue at a specific meeting.

**23ABC says the two candidates competing for a seat on the Arvin City Council, Susana Reyes and Lissette Medina, both put economic growth at the center of their campaigns.** Reyes, who joined the council in November 2022 and is seeking re-election, said she wants to focus on responsible spending, stronger infrastructure, public safety and meaningful opportunities for the community. Medina, an Arvin native raising her family there, said she realized she needed to stop waiting for change and start taking action; both told the station that building a strong foundation for Arvin’s economy is essential to its future.

**KGET 17 reports that the City of Bakersfield is preparing a possible new law that would hold property owners accountable for illegal fireworks set off on their property.** The move responds to continued complaints about fireworks noise and the risks they carry during holiday periods, and it would give the city another layer of enforcement beyond current rules. The report did not include details on penalties or when the ordinance might come before the council.

**According to 23ABC, Ward 3 City Council candidates Pedro Naveiras and Juan Carlos Llamas share very different views of what Bakersfield needs next.** Llamas said his campaign is not about left or right, and he prefers to focus on transparency for parents about what schools are teaching, as well as making affordable whole foods available to people in need. Naveiras, a prosecutor, said frustration with city council decisions on public safety is what drove him into the race, and he wants long-term maintenance and hiring plans that would boost police, fire and road crews. Five candidates are competing for the Ward 3 seat; previews of the remaining candidates are expected next week.

**KGET 17 reports that Rep. Josh Harder’s bill calling for the eradication and control of the invasive golden mussel has advanced in Congress.** The legislation targets a species that threatens California water infrastructure and could spread further through the Delta and into the Central Valley. The report did not specify the bill’s next legislative step.

## Something good

The inaugural Houchin “Gala to Give” raised more than $97,000, a strong start for a brand-new community event. The fundraiser shows how quickly local donors will support a worthy cause when they believe in the mission. Houchin organizers have to be pleased with the turnout and the total, and it sets a good foundation for the years to come.

## Coming up this week

The public calendar has a steady mix of meetings and nights out. Tonight, the city’s Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m., likely the main item of civic interest before the weekend. Monday at noon, the Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee holds its regular meeting, and Tuesday at noon the Homelessness panel convenes. At the Fox Theater, the entertainment line-up starts Friday night with It’s A 2000s Party: Bakersfield, followed Monday by the Cults & Classics screening of What Ever Happened to Baby Jane? Midweek brings Men I Trust with special guest Evan Wright on Wednesday, and Mike Sherm performs Saturday, Sept. 26. The theater also still has its Cults & Classics Season Pass for the 2026-2027 season, with Young Frankenstein scheduled for Oct. 5. Whether your week ends at a committee table or under the Fox marquee, there’s plenty to do before the month turns.
